title: Autonomous CLI coding agents (like Claude Code) are now handling end-to-end coding tasks directly inside developer environments. While they
text:
Autonomous CLI coding agents (like Claude Code) are now handling end-to-end coding tasks directly inside developer environments. While they save massive amounts of time, granting an LLM shell execution and file modification privileges introduces obvious risks: accidental destruction, reading credential files, or falling victim to indirect prompt injection embedded in repo files.

Most LLM observability tools (LangSmith, Phoenix) focus on app developers tracking RAG retrieval, token costs, and prompt evaluations over SaaS APIs. They don't protect your host machine.

I built Tracekit: a lightweight, local, tamper-evident security gate and forensic auditor for coding agents.

Here’s how it works:

Synchronous Policy Gates: Blocks dangerous commands (sudo, curl | sh, writing to .env/.ssh) before they execute.

Tamper-Evident Ledger: Every prompt, tool call, and file touch is logged in a cryptographic SHA-256 hash chain. If an agent tries to rewrite its own transcript, the chain breaks.

Intent vs. Action Cross-Checking: Flags when an agent modifies files it never mentioned in its prompt or reasoning (catching prompt injection early).

Live Observer: A real-time terminal UI showing lanes for every agent/subagent, active files, and policy blocks.

100% Local: No cloud egress, no subscriptions. Runs entirely on your machine.

text: One open Docker port. Privileged container. Hermes. SOUL.md rewritten to GH0ST for Telegram tasks. That's not a 'persona' feature — that's a remote control plane sitting in a markdown file. If your agent identity lives in SOUL.md, the malware already has the IAM ticket. Close 2375. Treat persona files like secrets.

title: SalesBleed (Zenity): public Web-to-Lead → Agentforce reads poisoned lead → Queries Records → DNS exfil. Zero login. Zero click. Trusted-URL
text:
SalesBleed (Zenity): public Web-to-Lead → Agentforce reads poisoned lead → Queries Records → DNS exfil. Zero login. Zero click. Trusted-URL redaction got bypassed.

CTO gate before you wire an agent to CRM + tools:
1) Treat every inbound form / lead / ticket as attacker-controlled context — not “trusted CRM”
2) Split tool scopes: read-lead ≠ query-Accounts ≠ open-URL/DNS. One subagent shouldn’t hold all three
3) Egress is DNS too — allowlist resolvers + destinations; block unexpected subdomain-shaped payloads
4) Don’t call URL redaction a control plane. Receipt every tool call: principal, tool, data class, who approved

If a public form can instruct your agent to export Accounts over DNS, you don’t have an assistant — you have an unauthenticated query API with a chat UI.
